transcript.text:
To help narrow this down, please check two things: 1. Is the door fully shut and clicking into place?
2. Is the drum still tumbling (turning) or is it stationary but the fan/motor running?
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check" — If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]
door is shut. the drum turns for a few seconds every couple of minutes after it says End, then stops again

[Heading: Probably normal cool-down cycle]
That behaviour is actually quite normal for many tumble dryers. After the programme finishes and displays 'End', the appliance often enters a cool-down phase to prevent clothes from getting creased while still hot. It is common for the drum to rotate intermittently (every few minutes) during this time to keep the load loose, even if the heating element has switched off. To confirm it isn't a fault: wait and see if it eventually powers down completely (lights out, fan stops) within 10–20 minutes. If it does, your dryer is working correctly. If it runs indefinitely without stopping or never turns off the fan/lights, please let me know.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
it carries on for about an hour if I leave the clothes in. stops when I open the door though. is that ok?

[Heading: Normal operation]
That is completely normal. Most tumble dryers are designed to keep running the fan and intermittent tumbling after the programme ends to cool down the clothes and prevent creasing. The door switch acts as a safety interlock: opening the door cuts power to the drum rotation (and often the heating) immediately, which explains why it stops when you open it. You can leave it to finish its cycle or simply open the door to stop it sooner if you need to remove the laundry.
